subject: Startups
title: Nokia: Rubber to Phones to Ruin
description: A fast breakdown of Nokia: Rubber to Phones to Ruin for builders.

hook.text: Nokia started as a paper mill in 1865. Then rubber boots. Then cables. Then it became the world's top phone maker.

buildup.text: By 2007, Nokia held 50% of global phone market share. They seemed untouchable and had billions in cash.

discovery.text: When the iPhone launched, Nokia dismissed touchscreens. They believed physical keyboards were what users wanted.

twist.text: Nokia's failure to pivot to smartphones cost them everything. Market share dropped from 50% to 3% in six years.

climax.text: Microsoft bought Nokia's phone division for $7 billion in 2013, then wrote off most of it as a loss.

punchline.text: The king of phones refused to pivot and lost the throne.

quiz.question: What was Nokia's original business in 1865?
